meaning: A kick on every beat of the bar, slots 0, 4, 8 and 12. House, techno and trance use it.
A note on a beat of the bar, where slot mod 4 is 0. Said alone, it may mean only slot 0.
The eighth-note 'and' between beats, where slot mod 4 is 2: slots 2, 6, 10 and 14.

ask.question: Does offbeat mean the eighth 'and', any off-beat sixteenth, or a psytrance bass line?
ask.when: The request asks for a psytrance bass line. Every other request takes the eighth 'and'.

meaning: Any sixteenth that is off the beat, where slot mod 4 is 1 or 3. Producers say 'offbeat 16ths' for it.
In a psytrance bass line, notes sit after the kick and never on it: one on the 'and' or three after the kick.
Snare or clap on beats 2 and 4, slots 4 and 12. It shows in 23 of 30 house and techno grids and 17 of 21 breakbeat grids.
The tempo stays and the snare or clap lands only on slot 8, beat 3. Kick sits on 0 with few extras, and hats and bass keep full-tempo density.

ask.question: Should half-time keep the tempo and move the snare to beat 3, or halve the tempo?

meaning: The tempo itself is halved, so the whole pattern runs at half speed.
In dance music, the same as the offbeat: the eighth 'and' at slots 2, 6, 10 and 14.
A pickup: notes in slots 12 to 15 of the bar before a phrase starts.
At least half of the onsets fall off the beat, where slot mod 4 is not 0.
The rhythm grid halves, so the pulse and the pattern run twice as fast at the same tempo. No single note rule carries this.
Three notes in the time of two. An eighth triplet starts at 0, 1/3 and 2/3 of a beat; a sixteenth triplet needs a 24-slot bar.
A note held one and a half times as long. A run of dotted eighths from slot 0 hits slots 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12.
A line that keeps going: at least 75 percent of the eighth or sixteenth slots filled, near-equal velocity and equal lengths.
Short notes of 0.25 to 0.5 beat pushed ahead of strong beats, at slot mod 4 of 2 or 3. The pushed note carries an accent of 100 or more.
A note that lands two sixteenths before a strong beat and is held across it: slots 6 and 14, ahead of beats 3 and 1.
An open hi-hat, played on the offbeat slots 2, 6, 10 and 14 as in house and trance.
No swing: the pair percent is 50 and every second note starts exactly on its slot.
A pair percent near 54 that only loosens a straight beat. The second sixteenth is about 8 percent of a sixteenth late.
Swung sixteenths at 58 to 62 percent, usually 58. The second sixteenth of each pair is 16 to 24 percent of a sixteenth late.
Swung eighths at 66.7 percent, a long note twice as long as the short one. Producers also call it a triplet shuffle.
Swung sixteenths at 75 percent, a long note three times as long as the short one.
Swung eighths at about 61 percent by default. The ratio is near 1 at fast tempo and near 3.5 at slow tempo. Real jazz files put the offbeat at 53 to 67 percent.
Swung sixteenth hats at about 59 to 64 percent, with extra hits at slot mod 4 of 1 and 3.
Eighth notes swung 2:1 (66.7 percent), the blues and jazz shuffle. With no genre named, take this sense.

ask.question: Is the shuffle an eighth-note swing, a garage sixteenth swing, or a whole drum pattern?
ask.when: The request names no genre. A named genre picks the sense: garage takes the sixteenth swing, blues and jazz take the eighth swing.

meaning: Sixteenth notes swung at 59 to 64 percent, as in UK garage.
A whole shuffled drum groove, not only a swing amount. The genre template supplies the pattern.
Snare and other backbeat hits land 10 to 25 ms late. Kick and bass stay on the grid.
Hits land 5 to 20 ms early, ahead of the grid.
Random drift in start times of 5 to 20 ms and in velocity of 5 to 12 per voice. Real drummers on a click vary by about 20 ms. Lengths do not change.
Tight dance timing: start times within 5 ms of the grid and velocity within 3 to 5.
A very quiet hit, velocity 20 to 45, usually on a snare at slot mod 4 of 1 or 3. Drum and bass puts ghost snares at 2, 7, 9 and 15.
A hit at velocity 100 to 127 among notes at 70 to 90. The sound only follows velocity when the preset routes velocity to level or cutoff.

controls.label: Velocity Track
controls.step: set above 0 percent so velocity changes the level

meaning: A soft hit, velocity 46 to 69.
A normal hit, velocity 70 to 99. Velocity 0 is a note-off and never a quiet note.
The feel of a pattern: its swing, its push and pull, and its accents together. No single note rule carries it.
The 3+3+2 figure, a Euclidean pattern of 3 onsets in 8 steps. One bar holds slots 0, 3, 6, 8, 11 and 14.
Kick on slots 0 and 10, snare on 4 and 12. Drum and bass runs it near 172 BPM and garage near 132.
One quarter note. Tempo is counted in quarter-note beats per minute and never in eighths.
Kick on every beat and snare on slots 3, 6, 11 and 14, at 88 to 100 BPM, with the 808 on the chord root.
The son clave in its 3-2 order: slots 0, 3, 6, 10 and 12.
The son clave in its 2-3 order: slots 2, 4, 8, 11 and 14.
The bossa pattern: slots 0, 3, 6, 10 and 13.
Beat 1 stays empty. Kick and rim play together only on slot 8, and the hats run on eighths.
Kick on slot 0 plus extras at 7 and 10, snare on 4 and 12. All 21 grids of the pattern set start with a kick at 0 and only one puts every kick on a beat.
A four-bar break. Bar 1 has kick on 0, 2, 10 and 11, snare on 4 and 12, quiet snares on 7, 9 and 15, and ride on eighths. Bars 3 and 4 delay the last snare an eighth.
Per beat, a long note then two short ones at +0, +0.5 and +0.75 beat, with lengths 0.5, 0.25 and 0.25. Staccato halves the lengths.
The reverse gallop: per beat two short notes then a long one at +0, +0.25 and +0.5 beat.
Trap hats on sixteenths, downbeats at velocity 100 to 127 and upbeats at 40 to 70. A roll of 3 to 4 hits rises in velocity into the snare, written as sixteenth triplets.
The tempo word largo: 41 to 60 BPM in a captioned MIDI set, median 58.
The tempo word adagio: 61 to 70 BPM in a captioned MIDI set, median 67.
The tempo word andante: 71 to 90 BPM in a captioned MIDI set, median 82.
The tempo word moderato: 91 to 110 BPM in a captioned MIDI set, median 100.
The tempo word allegro: 111 to 140 BPM in a captioned MIDI set, median 120.
The tempo word vivace: 141 to 160 BPM in a captioned MIDI set, median 150.
The tempo word presto: 161 to 210 BPM in a captioned MIDI set, median 180.
A caption phrase for tempos of 81 to 120 BPM. It overlaps the tempo words, so it gives a range.
A caption phrase for tempos of 121 to 160 BPM. It overlaps the tempo words, so it gives a range.
The rumba clave in its 3-2 order: slots 0, 3, 7, 10 and 12.
A Euclidean pattern of 5 onsets in 8 steps: steps 0, 2, 3, 5 and 6, which fill half a bar on a sixteenth grid.
A reggae drum feel. Two sources define it in opposite ways to steppers, so the dictionary keeps no pattern for it.
A reggae drum feel. Two sources define it in opposite ways to rockers, so the dictionary keeps no pattern for it.
The jungle tempo: about 130 BPM in 1990 and 170 to 180 BPM since 1996.
Two pulse groups of a and b notes against each other. They repeat every lcm(a, b)/a and lcm(a, b)/b pulses.
Two bar lengths played together. The pattern realigns after lcm(a, b) pulses.
Over six pulses the accents shift between 0 and 3 and 0, 2 and 4. Sources dispute the exact accents.
A rhythm of k onsets spread as evenly as possible over n steps. Pick k and n, and rotate only when a tradition is named.
